liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Never Trust A Woman** (2 reviews): Jerry was leaving after Terrapin when Brent started singing this; Jerry returned and strapped his guitar back on; Phil began leaving, limping, when Brent started this, then returned to his amp and played it with great force [20][25]
- **To Lay Me Down** (1 review): Rated among the ten best versions of To Lay Me Down [15]
- **Passenger** (1 review): Passenger, then a standard first-set tune, ripped; the reviewer wonders why it was retired after the 1981 New Year's run [15]
- **Samson & Delilah** (1 review): Samson opened with confidence, no hesitation, and Bobby's playing was restrained and well judged [21]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): After Terrapin's first instrumental section, a band member blanked on lyrics and Weir whispered them to him [14]
- **Space** (1 review): Mickey played the beam during Space, making the air shake at the Greek [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-09-13.148724.sbd.walker.scotton.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): soundboard; 26 songs; 192 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1981-09-13.sbd.miller.32576.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 26 songs; 188 min; rated 3.7/5 by 10 [3]. Said about its sound: The older circulating version was tinny with Phil washed out; this soundboard source is a solid improvement [19]
- **gd81-09-13.wise.munder.7092.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 25 songs; 183 min; rated 3.86/5 by 7 [4]. Said about its sound: The revving bike is audible on the audience tape during Drums, though quieter than it seemed live [17]
- **gd1981-09-13.148628.fob.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 26 songs; 188 min [5]

## Around the show

- A Hells Angel rode a motorcycle onto the stage, wiped it down and revved the engine during Drums; theater vibrations shook [17]
- The crowd danced and watched the sun set over the bay while the band played [20]
- The motorcycle during the drum solo was extremely loud in person; homemade hot air balloons were also released at this show [22]
- Fans stood throughout apart from the set break; it was a beautiful day with the sun setting over the rocks [23]
- Phil was limping late in the show, though he hadn't been during the first set [25]
- Judged a very nice show, though not as monstrous as the previous day's, closing the first Greek run [15]
- Third night of the run: the 11th was spacey and nocturnal, the 12th hard-driving, this one a mellow afternoon show [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-09-13.148724.sbd.walker.scotton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Master Soundboard Cassette > Cassette [1]. Also: Mark Severson's Nakamichi 700 front-of-board source patches part of Loser, end of Terrapin, all of Never Trust A Woman, Drums and Brokedown Palace [1]
- **gd1981-09-13.sbd.miller.32576.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Set 1: SBD -> Cassette Master -> ? -> Cassette -> Sound Forge -> CD; Set 2: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Cassette [3]. Also: Set 2 came from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker; set 1 from Jeff Harrison and Jake Feinberg; Jim Wise's audience recording supplies patches; the Senn 421 cassette master patches Jack Straw, Loser, Terrapin, Never Trust A Woman and Drums [3]
- **gd81-09-13.wise.munder.7092.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jim Wise; source: Audience Recording: Sennheiser 421's [4]. Also: Passed via Nic Brokenleg and Kevin Gills, then converted to SHN with EAC by Willy [4]
- **gd1981-09-13.148628.fob.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; 3 x Nakamichi 700 mics (cardioid left & right - X pattern; 80 degree angle; 6db bass EQ, omni center pointed… [5]. Also: Bob Wagner and Charlie Miller's Nakamichi 700 source supplies an 11-second patch in Drums; The Wheel includes its space [5]
